name: Acmer S2 Pro 48W
tagline: Top Acmer S2 Pro: 48W compressed diode with bundle options
tldr: Acmer S2 Pro 48W is Acmer's high-power open-frame option before the enclosed P3. Strong cutting claims: verify optical power and compare to P3 48W enclosed if you need smoke control.
mainObjective: Maximum cut speed and depth in the line: engraving remains strong at tuned speeds

engraveExample.description: Filled photo or logo on birch plywood

cutExample.description: Simple square cut-out from 3 mm basswood

pros: Widest cut range of the S2 Pro line in our profile: basswood up to 10 mm and dark acrylic up to 5 mm
Fastest fills of the line: ~12–18 min for our 10 × 10 cm photo test
Built-in 30 L/min air pump, so the extra power translates into cleaner cuts without add-ons
cons: $759.99 for the basic pack vs $582 for the 36W, and up to $1,404.99 for the All in One pack (October 2026)
Same 0.08 × 0.1 mm spot spec as the 36W: no gain in detail, and more smoke at full power
Open frame: if smoke control matters, compare Acmer's enclosed P3 before buying
beginnerNotes: This profile is the 48W SKU on Acmer S2 Pro. Read the TL;DR and benchmarks above, then compare other power options via the chips before buying.
proTips: The 48W head is for cut-heavy weeks: air assist, exhaust, and multi-pass squares on your plywood before you raise customer prices. Dial engraving speeds down when photo quality beats throughput.

editorialDepth.advantages: Acmer S2 Pro 48W targets mixed engraving and wood-cutting weeks: fewer passes on basswood and dark acrylic than weaker SKUs in the same line.
editorialDepth.limitations: Wrong pick if you never engrave and only wanted the lowest price. Ultra-fine photo work can look better on an engraving-first SKU. Open-frame: safety and smoke are on you.

faq.question: Is the S2 Pro 48W worth $178 more than the 36W?
faq.answer: If cutting is a weekly task, generally yes. In our benchmarks it cuts a 10 × 10 cm square in 3 mm basswood in ~6–10 min (vs ~7–12 min) and fills a photo in ~12–18 min (vs ~14–22 min). Acmer's basic packs were $759.99 and $582 in October 2026. For engraving only, the 36W gives the same detail for less.

faq.question: What thickness should I expect to cut with the 48W?
faq.answer: Acmer gives no official cutting chart for the S2 Pro. Our profile lists basswood up to 10 mm and opaque dark acrylic up to 5 mm, with several passes at the top of those ranges; clear acrylic is not possible with a blue diode.

faq.question: Does more power mean a coarser engraving?
faq.answer: Not on paper: Acmer specifies the same 0.08 × 0.1 mm spot for both S2 Pro versions. In practice you will run lower power percentages on the 48W for photos, and smoke and charring rise at full power, so air assist (built in) and an exhaust matter more.

standoutFeatures.title: Top cutting tier of the S2 Pro
standoutFeatures.body: Basswood up to 10 mm and dark acrylic up to 5 mm in our profile, with the shortest cut times of the line (~6–10 min for our 3 mm test square).

standoutFeatures.title: Integrated 30 L/min air assist
standoutFeatures.body: The built-in pump clears smoke at the cut, which matters more at 48W where charring rises quickly.
